On the second leg of the visit to the state, the Senate committee visited some markets and sites of on-going road projects.
At the state capital, Governor Akeredolu received the Committee and conveyed profound joy over the swift rehabilitation of the federal roads, emphasizing that the state government made this decision to alleviate the peoples' suffering and enhance commercial activities for citizens.
The governor examined the ongoing reconstruction of the Ondo, Araromi, Irun Akoko, Irele-Iwaro road, highlighting the 40-kilometer segment as a crucial Federal Road linking the state’s commercial activities.
Senator Gaya led the Committee team to inspect several ongoing projects in the state, including City Market, Fine and Dandy, Ajaokuta, and International market in Akure, stating that the renovated ones were exemplary models of well-done roads.
Receiving the Committee members in his office at the Government House, Akure, Arakunrin Akeredolu, appreciated the federal lawmakers for the visit and commended their doggedness in ensuring the well-being of the people.
He applauded the senators for moving round the country to ascertain in a very practical way the condition of the federal roads, especially as they had earlier inspected the ones in Osun State.
The Governor said the possible future federal intervention would open more opportunities in agriculture, tourism, commercial activities and all other aspects of the social economy of the state.
He made it known that the state is desperate at having a good Federal Road to the commercial city of Ondo, stressing the need to rehabilitate the markets centres.
Mr. Doyin Olatuyi, Chairman of Ise Oluwa market, revealed that the market, being the largest in Ondo State, faced significant challenges due to potholed roads that hindered both the movement of goods and customer traffic, ultimately disorganizing the market.
